bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar tough test for BJP's UCC plan as JD(U) seeks talks amid differing voices
bihar_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s call to implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) by 2029 in BJP-NDA-ruled states has triggered a fresh political fault line in Bihar, with the ruling JD(U) ruling out its implementation in the state. While Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) and Hindustani Awam Morcha have backed the move, the Rashtriya Lok Morcha has not yet made its position on the UCC clear. Advertisement The development has also drawn sharp criticism from the principal Opposition RJD, which has accused the BJP of using the UCC to advance its political agenda and warned that it would affect people of all religions. Advertisement While the BJP has maintained that the UCC would be implemented only after consultations with all alliance partners, the divergent positions within the NDA have brought the issue back into the centre of Bihar’s political discourse. Reacting to Amit Shah’s statement, veteran JD(U) leader and MLA Shyam Rajak said that his party had indeed supported legislation related to the UCC in Parliament, but had also made it clear at the time that it would not be implemented in Bihar. He said that the JD(U)’s position on Bihar had been clear earlier and remains unchanged. Meanwhile, JD(U) National Working President Sanjay Jha said that he would soon meet the Union Home Minister to discuss the UCC implementation in Bihar. However, he didn’t clarify whether his party was fully in support of the UCC or there is still more to discuss on the issue. On the JD(U)’s opposition, senior BJP leader Ram Kripal Yadav said that all aspects would be deliberated upon and a decision would be taken only after taking all parties into confidence. However, he also said that if Amit Shah had made the statement, then it was likely to happen. RJD spokesperson Ejaz Ahmed said that the UCC amounts to advancing the BJP’s political agenda. He said that it would affect people of all religions and weaken the Constitution and constitutional rights. Congress spokesperson Asitnath Tiwari said that several states across the country are currently facing severe floods and that the affected people need assistance. He said that the country’s leaders should first take care of the welfare and basic needs of the people and stop “beating the drum” about the UCC. bihar_raw_news.content: Muzaffarpur, Sep 14: Two labourers died of asphyxiation while they were removing shuttering from a newly constructed septic tank in Bihar’s Muzaffarpur district on Monday, officials said. The incident occurred in the Sikandarpur police station area of the district. The deceased have been identified as Sonu Kumar and Mohammad Jahangir. Labourers die during work “The two labourers entered the tank to remove the shuttering, but subsequently died of asphyxiation. bihar_raw_news.title: Transforming animal husbandry, empowering rural Odisha - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Transforming animal husbandry, empowering rural Odisha Updated: 5 hours, 52 min ago Bhubaneswar (Odisha), September 14 (ANI): For millions of rural families in Odisha, animal husbandry has always been part of everyday life. Today, the sector is emerging as a powerful engine of livelihoods, income generation, employment and rural economic growth. Under the leadership of Hon’ble Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Odisha is building a stronger and more productive livestock economy through targeted schemes, financial support, modern infrastructure and improved veterinary services. At the heart of this transformation is the Mukhyamantri Kamdhenu Yojana, with a substantial budget outlay of Rs. 1,423 crore, aimed at increasing daily milk production and benefiting more than 15 lakh dairy farmers across the state. Under the Gopalan Yojana and Buffalo Entrepreneurship Development Scheme, farmers receive 60 to 70 per cent subsidy for establishing dairy units, enabling them to expand livestock-based livelihoods and participate in a growing dairy economy. Animal welfare remains a priority. Under the Mukhyamantri Prani Kalyan Yojana, 13 new Goshalas were constructed during 2025-26, providing shelter for around 1,100 stray animals, while 97 Goshalas received feeding and maintenance support covering more than 25,000 stray and destitute animals. Verma, along with two other members. Curated by Mansi Image: File photo Sep 14, 2026 Share The Bihar government has set up a high-level committee to examine the existing process for recruiting assistant professors in state universities and suggest changes to the system. The move follows weeks of protests by PhD holders and researchers who have sought changes in the recruitment process, including a higher upper age limit and objective-type written examinations. According to PTI, the committee will review various aspects of assistant professor recruitment and recommend reforms to the current system. Panel to review assistant professor recruitment process The committee includes retired IAS officers Amarjit Sinha and Sanjay Kumar, physicist and Padma Shri awardee Professor H.C. Verma, along with two other members. Sanjay Kumar, additional secretary (university) in the Governor's Secretariat, will serve as the member secretary of the committee. Dipak Kumar Singh, additional chief secretary to the Governor, announced the formation of the panel on Saturday. The committee will examine several parts of the existing recruitment process. These include the upper age limit, eligibility criteria, examination and interview formats, and the weightage given to different selection parameters. The panel will also consider matters related to guest lecturers and other issues connected with the recruitment system before proposing changes. Committee formed after agreement with researchers' association The committee was formed following an agreement reached on August 24 between Bihar Governor Lt Gen (Retd) Ata Hasnain and representatives of the All PhD Holders and Researchers Association, according to PTI. The association had demanded changes to the assistant professor recruitment system and held a three-week protest in Patna last month. The demonstrations took place at Gardani Bagh, the designated protest venue in the state capital. Some participants also went on hunger strikes during the protest. PhD holders demand higher age limit, objective tests One of the association's main demands was to raise the maximum age limit for appointment as an assistant professor to 55 years. The protesters also called for objective-type written examinations as part of the recruitment process. The agitation ended after representatives of the association held a two-hour meeting with Governor Hasnain. During the meeting, the Governor assured the delegation that a committee of educationists and administrators would be formed within 15 days to consider their demands, PTI reported. Panel to examine wider recruitment reforms The committee's work will cover more than the specific demands raised by the protesters. It will assess the wider structure of assistant professor recruitment and recommend changes based on its findings. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar becomes first state in India to launch dedicated investment policy for sugar industry
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News AI Representational Image Patna: In what is being described as a first-of-its-kind initiative in the country, the Bihar government has announced a direct grant of Rs 14 crore per year for five consecutive years to investors who set up new sugar mills in the state, taking the total payout to Rs 70 crore per mill over five years. The move is part of the newly launched Bihar Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy-2026, which came into force just a few days ago, The Times of India reported. State Sugarcane Commissioner Anil Kumar Jha confirmed to media that the grant will be disbursed in equal annual instalments of Rs 14 crore, with the first instalment released just one month after the new mill begins operations. To be eligible, a new sugar mill must have a minimum crushing capacity of 3,500 tonnes per day. Investors looking to go beyond the base capacity will find additional incentives waiting. For every extra 100 tonnes of crushing capacity added above the 3,500 tonne threshold, the government will provide an additional Rs 2 crore, making larger investments progressively more attractive. The policy also addresses one of the most significant challenges for new industrial projects – land. The government has linked land support directly to the size of the plant. An investor setting up a mill with a capacity of 5,000 tonnes per day will be eligible for up to 40 acres of land on lease at a token payment of just Re 1. For a mill at the minimum capacity of 3,500 tonnes per day, up to 25 acres will be made available on the same terms. On top of this, the policy provides full reimbursement of registration fees and stamp duty on land purchased for setting up new sugar mills. The policy does not stop at new investments. Existing and operational sugar mills looking to expand their capacity will also benefit. The government will provide Rs 15 crore for a capacity expansion of 1,000 tonnes per day, with an additional Rs 1.5 crore offered for every further 100 tonnes of expansion beyond that. What sets this policy apart from those of other states, according to Jha, is that Bihar has created a standalone investment promotion framework exclusively for the sugarcane industry. Every other state in the country, he said, folds sugarcane-related incentives into broader industrial policies. Bihar’s decision to carve out a separate policy for this sector is being seen as a strong signal of the state government’s intent to revive and grow its sugar industry. Jha also said that the incentives and land support on offer in Bihar are more generous than what any other state currently provides. The government has set an ambitious target behind this policy – to establish 25 new sugar mills across Bihar and restart nine mills that have been shut down, all within the next five years. The policy is also expected to generate employment for one crore youth in the state

bihar_raw_news.title: Green Municipal Bonds To Raise ₹10,000 Crore In India Over Next 30 Months As Cities ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Mumbai, Sep 14: Civic bodies in India are likely to raise Rs 10,000 crore through the green municipal bonds route over the next 30 months, a report said on Monday. Pegging the required urban infrastructure investments at over Rs 56 lakh crore during FY27-30, domestic rating agency Icra said up to Rs 3 lakh crore of this amount will be raised from commercial debt financing route, which highlights the role of municipal and green bonds. The unavailability of projects, which can qualify for green finance, is "unlikely to be primary constraint" on the development of the green municipal bond market, it said, pointing out that water supply, sewerage and wastewater treatment, solid waste management, renewable energy and climate-resilient infrastructure qualify. Around a fourth of the Rs 6,540 crore raised through the municipal bonds route qualify as green municipal bonds while another fourth have the potential to be treated as green, it said. "We estimate a base-case green municipal bond issuance potential of Rs 10,000 crore over FY2027-FY2030, with further upside as issuer readiness improves," it said. Stating that supply-side constraints are a key challenge for the development of this instrument, it said municipalities with adequate credit quality, proper financial disclosures, repayment visibility, project preparation and transaction readiness will be the ones who can access the capital market in a sustainable manner. "...market-access filters will materially reduce the investible issuer universe despite the broader infrastructure requirement," it pointed out. Recent issues have shown a readiness among investors to subscribe to such green bond issuances, it said, adding that recent green bond subscriptions have witnessed a 5-times over-subscription. Moreover, the green bond issuances have continued to offer a visible yield premium of up to 1.90 per cent over the sovereign and up to 1.55 per cent over the state benchmarks, it added. "These trends indicate that investor appetite for municipal green finance is developing, while supply-side constraints remain a more significant impediment for market expansion than capital availability," it said. The rating agency acknowledged that policy support and market development initiatives are "gradually addressing" the supply-side barriers. bihar_raw_news.title: India Approves Up To 654 MW Power Export To Nepal After Floods Damage Hydropower ...
bihar_raw_news.content: New Delhi [India], September 14: The Ministry of Power has approved the export of up to 654 MW of electricity to Nepal from September 13 to December 31 to help the neighbouring country meet its power requirements following damage to hydropower infrastructure caused by recent devastating flash floods. The approval allows power export for 18 hours a day, from 0000 hours to 1800 hours, to the Nepal Electricity Authority, the Ministry of Power said. According to the Ministry, up to 600 MW of power can be exported through the Muzaffarpur-Dhalkebar 400 kV D/c line, while up to 54 MW can be exported through the Tanakpur-Mahendranagar 132 kV S/c line. Export of Power to Nepal Approved ❇️ Ministry of Power has accorded approval for the export of power, for 18 hours a day (00:00 hours to 18:00 hours) to Nepal Electricity Authority from 13 September 2026 to 31 December, 2026. ❇️ Approval has been given for upto 600MW of export… pic.twitter.com/wUgwtgKvug — PIB India (@PIB_India) September 14, 2026 Power export approval details "The quantum of power to be exported from January 2027 will be reviewed in December 2026," the Ministry of Power said in a release. The Ministry said the recent floods in Nepal have caused significant damage to hydropower infrastructure, reducing the country's domestic power generation capacity and creating an additional requirement for electricity. "The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and longstanding energy cooperation between India and Nepal," the Ministry said. The Ministry further said that India remains committed to supporting Nepal and strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector. Against the backdrop of the mounting toll, India has continued to support Nepal's rescue, relief and forensic operations, with an eighth Indian Air Force flight carrying humanitarian assistance reaching Kathmandu earlier. Earlier, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that India has expedited the delivery of relief supplies, specialised equipment and expert personnel through eight special flights since August 26, sending more than 130 tonnes of relief material to Nepal. Also Watch: Relief operations continue India has also deployed 54 expert personnel to support Nepal's ongoing rescue, relief and forensic operations, the MEA said in a statement issued on September 9. The assistance includes standard relief supplies such as temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits, solar lamps and medicines, besides specialised equipment for tunnel and mud rescue operations, DNA profiling and other emergency requirements. bihar_raw_news.title: Floods hit 4.9 million people in 15 Bihar districts as rivers keep swelling - Business Standard
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India News / Floods hit 4.9 million people in 15 Bihar districts as rivers keep swelling Floods hit 4.9 million people in 15 Bihar districts as rivers keep swelling The local weather office said the state has recorded 111.7 mm of rain so far in September, around 13 per cent above normal Patna: An aerial view of the flood-affected Didarganj area inundated by the swollen Ganga river, in Patna, Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026.(Photo:PTI) Press Trust of India Patna 2 min read Last Updated : Sep 14 2026 | 12:46 PM IST Listen to This Article More than 4.9 million people in 15 districts of Bihar were affected by floods on Monday as heavy rain over the past few days further swelled the rivers of the state already flowing above their danger marks. The local weather office said the state has recorded 111.7 mm of rain so far in September, around 13 per cent above normal. An official said incessant rain in catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar and heavy rainfall in the state itself have caused several rivers and streams to flow above their danger marks. According to the Disaster Management Department, around 4.936 million people in 15 districts have been affected by floods. These districts are Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria. The Kosi river was flowing above the danger mark at Baltara and Kursela, the Budhi Gandak at Khagaria, the Ganga at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger, the Punpun at Sripalpur, the Bagmati at Benibad, and the Ghaghara at Darauli. The administration was operating 1,260 community kitchens and 13 relief camps in flood-affected areas. Accommodation, food, medical care and other essential arrangements have been made for around 11,060 people, it said. The Disaster Management Department said the barrage over the Gandak river in Valmiki Nagar recorded a discharge of 90,600 cusecs of water at 10 am Monday, with the trend rising. The Kosi Barrage at Birpur recorded 1,51,015 cusecs of water discharge, against this year's peak of 2,55,425 cusecs on July 20. Twenty-seven teams of the State Disaster Response Force and 10 of the National Disaster Response Force have been deployed in various districts to aid in relief and rescue operations. national_raw_news.content: BRICS leaders have stressed that energy security is a crucial foundation for social and economic development, national security and the welfare of all nations. During the two day BRICS summit held in New Delhi, the member nations highlighted the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and protection of critical energy infrastructure. During the Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi cautioned that the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could become a hurdle to progress. India hosted the summit under the theme Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, placing people-centred development and the interests of the Global South at the heart of its presidency. The most significant outcome of the BRICS summit was the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration, which outlined the shared position on major geopolitical and economic issues. On the situation in West Asia, BRICS leaders called for maximum restraint, dialogue and diplomacy, and stressed the need to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure. The leaders strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and reiterated their commitment to a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism. A consensus was reached on a ‘BRICS Integrated Early Warning System’ for the prevention of and response to infectious diseases. This summit was highly significant from the perspective of global politics, the economy, and multilateral cooperation.

In its latest annual report 2025-26, the Defence Ministry said that these efforts have led to a significant decline in violence, a reduction in protests, and zero incidents of stone pelting. According to the report, the situation within Jammu and Kashmir and along the Line of Control had significantly altered during Operation Sindoor. However, after the Director Generals of Military Operations level talks last year, the situation has stabilised to a large extent, though the unpredictability continues. The report also highlighted the overall situation with China. The year 2025 witnessed a significant reduction in the deployment of China’s People Liberation Army (PLA) Forces opposite the Northern Borders, with 10 Combined Arms Brigade-sized forces each deployed in areas along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and in traditional training areas. The bilateral interactions between India and China at political, diplomatic and military levels facilitated positive developments along the Northern Borders, leading to stability. According to the report, the deployment of the Indian Army in all sectors along the LAC is robust, well-poised, and prepared to deal with any emerging contingency. The report also highlighted that the Defence Ministry is actively prioritizing the Indian industrial base to reduce dependency on foreign imports. Accordingly, a significant portion of the defence expenditure is directed inward boosting the local economy and defence infrastructure. Out of Total Defence Procurement approximately 75 percent was spent specifically for domestic procurement.

national_raw_news.title: India wins record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, President Murmu congratulates team 7 hours ago 244
national_raw_news.content: India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament. India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match. India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title. President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan also congratulated the team on lifting the Women’s T20 Asia Cup for a record eighth time. He said that the team’s unbeaten campaign, exceptional teamwork and unwavering determination throughout the tournament have brought immense pride to the nation. He also wished the players well for their future endeavours. Prime Minister Modi said that the confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit of the players were on full display throughout the tournament. Congratulating the Women’s team, Mr Modi wished that this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has congratulated the Indian women’s cricket team via a social media post. Mr Birla lauded the team for remaining unbeaten throughout the tournament and securing victory in the Asia Cup for the 8th time. He added that the cricketers gave a splendid demonstration of their talent and determination in the tournament and this victory is a triumph of the strength, hard work, and dreams of the daughters of India. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that the accomplishment inspires the youth of the country, to dream big, work hard, and move forward with full determination to achieve their goals.

national_raw_news.title: DRI busts Pakistan-origin imports; Seizes over 362 MT dry dates in Nashik - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: DRI busts Pakistan-origin imports; Seizes over 362 MT dry dates in Nashik Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर DRI busts Pakistan-origin imports; Seizes over 362 MT dry dates in Nashik ANI | Updated: Sep 14, 2026 16:49 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 14 (ANI): The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized more than 362 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin dry dates under 'Operation Deep Manifest' during an enforcement drive targeting illicit trade conduits. Acting on specific actionable intelligence, operational teams intercepted 13 cargo containers carrying the consignments at CFS Ambad in Nashik , which a Mumbai-based commercial entity imported. According to the Ministry of Finance, the shipments arrived via Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, accompanied by import clearance paperwork that falsely declared the UAE as the sovereign country of origin. Official findings revealed that the commercial consignment moved through a deliberate routing network designed to mask its true origin. The cargo started its maritime transit from Karachi Port in Pakistan, reaching Jebel Ali Port in the UAE aboard an initial vessel. "Preliminary investigation revealed a carefully orchestrated transhipment arrangement designed to conceal the Pakistan-origin of the goods," the Ministry stated. The operational breakdown showed that the illicit cargo underwent minimal physical handling in the Gulf transit hub to obscure the paper trail. "The dry dates were initially shipped from Karachi Port, Pakistan, to Jebel Ali Port, UAE, in one set of containers aboard one vessel," the official statement noted. Handlers in the transit zone then re-routed the shipment onto another carrier line, it stated. "At Jebel Ali, the goods were merely transshipped and transferred to another set of containers and loaded onto a different vessel for onward shipment to India through entities operated by Pakistani nationals," the Ministry confirmed. Border and port enforcement tightened following regulatory revisions enacted by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) in mid-2025. The Ministry mentioned that following the Pahalgam terror attack, the Government of India, in the interest of national security, imposed a complete prohibition on the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, with effect from 2 May 2025, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025. To counter non-compliant import tactics across container terminals, central enforcement authorities launched structured surveillance protocols targeting third-party trade jurisdictions. "In response, DRI, under 'Operation Deep Manifest', has been consistently identifying, intercepting and seizing Pakistan-origin goods attempted to be imported into India through third-country routing," the Ministry said. Customs and intelligence officials continue to track intermediate entities connected to commercial paper falsification, fraudulent routing manifests, and proxy transhipment nodes. "The seizure underscores DRI’s sustained resolve to identify, disrupt and dismantle sophisticated networks seeking to circumvent trade prohibitions through misdeclaration, transhipment and manipulation of documentation, thereby safeguarding national security and straightening supply chain integrity," the Ministry added. Convening on the landmark 20th anniversary of BRICS under the theme Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability , the summit produced a comprehensive 140-point consensus. BRICS New Delhi Declaration About BRICS New Delhi Declaration : What it is? The 18th BRICS Summit marks the institutionalization of the expanded grouping, consolidating cooperation across its three primary pillars: Political and Security Cooperation Economic and Financial Cooperation Cultural and People-to-People Exchanges Under the 2026 Indian presidency, the grouping organized over 400 ministerial, official, and technical meetings across 30 Indian cities, anchoring initiatives in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a people-centric, balanced, and development-oriented Global South agenda. Key Highlights of the New Delhi Declaration: Reforming Global Multilateral Institutions & the UN: Reaffirmed commitment to comprehensive UN reform, including expanding developing-country representation in the UN Security Council (UNSC) to reflect contemporary multipolar realities. Explicitly recognized the aspirations of African nations as reflected in the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration . Reasserted support from permanent members China and Russia for the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council. Noted that in the history of the United Nations, no woman has ever been elected Secretary-General , while calling for equitable geographical representation across senior international agency appointments without state monopolies. Bretton Woods & International Trade Reforms: Called for expedited quota increases under the IMF’s 16th General Review of Quotas (GRQ) and urgent, meaningful quota realignments under the 17th GRQ based on the Diriyah Guiding Principles to reflect the true economic weight of Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs). Advocated for the immediate restoration of a fully functional, two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism and the prompt appointment of Appellate Body members. Strongly opposed unilateral protectionist tariffs and non-tariff trade barriers, particularly highlighting that measures such as Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms (CBAM) distort trade and penalize developing nations under the guise of environmental goals. Endorsed the accession bids of Ethiopia and Iran to the WTO . Counter-Terrorism & Security Priorities: Condemned terrorism in all forms and manifestations, reiterating zero tolerance and rejecting double standards. Specifically condemned the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on April 22, 2025 , which claimed 26 lives. Called for the swift finalization and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism (CCIT) within the UN framework and coordinated multilateral action against all UN-designated terrorist entities. Welcomed the Guwahati Declaration adopted by the BRICS Heads of Anti-Drug Agencies to coordinate counter-narcotics operations. national_raw_news.title: India-China border: PLA deployment along LAC reduced in 2025, says Defence Ministry
national_raw_news.content: China Cuts PLA Troops Along LAC, Says Defence Ministry | Mathrubhumi English Home page » News » India » Line Of Actual Control India-China border: PLA deployment along LAC reduced in 2025, says Defence Ministry Edited By: Aiswarya Venugopal Last Updated: 14 September 2026, 10:13 AM IST A view of the road on the way to the Line of Actual Control, at the India-China Border in Tawang, in the northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh | Photo: AP New Delhi: China reduced the deployment of its People’s Liberation Army (PLA) forces along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in 2025, while renewed political, diplomatic and military engagement between India and China helped bring greater stability to the northern borders, according to the Defence Ministry’s latest annual report. The report said the PLA had 10 Combined Arms Brigade-size forces deployed in areas along the LAC, while another 10 such forces were stationed in traditional training areas. At the same time, the Indian Army maintained a robust deployment across all sectors of the LAC and remained prepared to deal with any emerging contingency, the ministry said. The assessment comes after the disengagement process along the India-China border and a renewed push by both sides to stabilise ties following years of military tensions. ALSO READ: India-China border fake videos circulate online; PIB warns against unverified LAC claims India-China border talks resume The Defence Ministry said bilateral engagement at the political, diplomatic and military levels contributed to positive developments along the northern borders during 2025. The two countries resumed meetings under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC), with the 33rd and 34th rounds held in March and July 2025. India and China also resumed talks between their Special Representatives on the boundary question, with two rounds taking place in December 2024 and August 2025. The renewed diplomatic engagement was accompanied by continued military-level discussions aimed at managing issues along the disputed border. ALSO READ: Satellite imagery exposes China’s encroachment in areas south of Doklam Military commanders hold talks in Eastern Ladakh The process also extended to the ground level, with the two armies continuing Border Personnel Meetings across all sectors. According to the Defence Ministry, these meetings continued in a cordial and friendly environment and were used to address issues of concern between Indian and Chinese forces. Another major engagement highlighted in the report was the 23rd Corps Commander Level Meeting, held in Eastern Ladakh on October 25 and 26, 2025. The ministry described the meeting as the senior-most military commander-level engagement and said the discussions reflected the constructive direction of India-China relations. Modi's China visit reinforced improving ties The Defence Ministry also pointed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to China for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Tianjin in August 2025 as another development that reinforced the improvement in bilateral relations. The combination of high-level political engagement, diplomatic talks and military dialogue contributed to what the ministry described as stability along the northern borders. national_raw_news.title: PIB Press Tour offers Arunachal journos a glance into innovation, infrastructure & cultural heritage
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News PIB Press Tour offers Arunachal journos a glance into innovation, infrastructure & cultural heritage | Tapan Kr DAS | ITANAGAR, Sep 13: A Press Information Bureau (PIB), Itanagar-sponsored press tour to Gujarat provided a nine-member media delegation from Arunachal Pradesh with an opportunity to explore a diverse range of development initiatives, institutions, technological innovations and cultural landmarks from September 6 to 12. The first-of-its-kind exposure visit for Arunachal-based journalists was designed to familiarise the media with major projects and institutions shaping Gujarat’s development landscape. It also enabled the participating journalists to interact with officials, experts and stakeholders and gain a first-hand understanding of initiatives in infrastructure, urban planning, technology, industry, education, transportation, cooperative development and heritage conservation. Led by PIB Itanagar Joint Director Utsav Parmar, the delegation travelled across Ahmedabad, Dholera, Vadodara and Ekta Nagar, witnessing the State’s efforts to combine economic growth with technological advancement, institutional development and cultural preservation. Exploring Gandhian heritage and urban development The tour began in Ahmedabad with a visit to Kochrab Ashram, a site closely associated with Mahatma Gandhi’s early experiments in community living, self-reliance and public service. The visit offered the journalists an insight into the historical and philosophical foundations of the freedom movement and the continuing relevance of Gandhian values. The delegation also visited the Sabarmati Riverfront, an important urban development project that has transformed the riverfront into a public space incorporating recreation, civic amenities and environmental improvement, and boosting tourism. The visit provided an opportunity to observe how urban infrastructure can be planned alongside public access and city beautification. At CEPT University, Ahmedabad, the journalists were introduced to perspectives on architecture, urban planning, design and sustainable development. The interaction helped connect the broader themes of infrastructure creation and urban growth with the importance of planning, design and academic research. Dholera: A glimpse of the emerging industrial landscape One of the major highlights of the tour was the visit to the Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR), Gujarat, a greenfield development project envisioned as a major industrial and investment destination. The delegation explored the emerging infrastructure and industrial ecosystem of Dholera and gained an understanding of the planning and connectivity requirements involved in developing a modern industrial region. The visit offered insights into the role of integrated infrastructure, technology and investment facilitation in attracting industries and creating new economic opportunities. For the visiting journalists, Dholera presented a practical example of how large-scale development projects are conceived and implemented, and how emerging industrial centres can contribute to employment generation, investment and regional growth. The visit also included an external view of Tata’s semiconductor fabrication plant, described as India’s first large-scale semiconductor fabrication facility, which is currently under construction at Dholera.
